description: Human-readable descriptions for the system tag taxonomy, keyed by Tag.ExternalKey. The seeder syncs these onto system-owned tags at every startup.

descriptions.Blues: African American roots music built on blue notes, call-and-response and the twelve-bar form, born in the Deep South.
descriptions.Brass & Military: Music for brass bands, marching bands and military ensembles, often written for parades and ceremonies.
descriptions.Children's: Music and audio made for children, from songs and lullabies to stories.
descriptions.Classical: Western art music from the medieval era to today, from solo pieces to full orchestras.
descriptions.Electronic: Music made mainly with synthesizers, drum machines, samplers and computers, from dance floors to sound art.
descriptions.Folk, World, & Country: Traditional and regional music from around the world, plus American folk and country.
descriptions.Funk / Soul: African American music built on deep grooves, soulful vocals and tight rhythm sections.
descriptions.Hip Hop: Rhythmic music built on beats and rapping, born in the Bronx in the 1970s.
descriptions.Jazz: Improvised, swing-rooted music born in New Orleans, from big bands to the avant-garde.
descriptions.Latin: Music from Latin America and the Caribbean, rich in rhythm, percussion and dance.
descriptions.Non-Music: Spoken word, sound effects, field recordings and other audio that is not primarily music.
descriptions.Pop: Catchy, accessible popular music built around hooks, melodies and vocals.
descriptions.Reggae: Jamaican music with an offbeat skank, heavy bass and roots in ska and rocksteady.
descriptions.Rock: Guitar-driven music with strong rhythms and attitude, from 1950s rock and roll to metal and indie.
descriptions.Stage & Screen: Music written for theatre, film, television and other productions.
descriptions.Blues---Boogie Woogie: Driving, dance-ready piano blues with a rolling eight-to-the-bar left hand.
descriptions.Blues---Chicago Blues: Amplified postwar blues from Chicago with electric guitar, harmonica and a full rhythm section.
descriptions.Blues---Country Blues: Early acoustic blues from the rural South, sung by solo performers with guitar.
descriptions.Blues---Delta Blues: Raw Mississippi Delta blues with slide guitar and intense, personal vocals.
descriptions.Blues---East Coast Blues: Blues from the Atlantic seaboard, often lighter and ragtime-tinged with fingerpicked guitar.
descriptions.Blues---Electric Blues: Blues played on amplified guitars, from the 1940s onward.
descriptions.Blues---Harmonica Blues: Blues led by harmonica, often amplified and bent into wailing, horn-like lines.
descriptions.Blues---Jump Blues: Up-tempo, horn-driven 1940s blues from the big band world and a direct ancestor of rock and roll.
descriptions.Blues---Louisiana Blues: Laid-back Louisiana blues with a swampy groove, echoey production and Cajun and R&B touches.
descriptions.Blues---Memphis Blues: Blues from Memphis, from early jug bands to the punchy electric sound of Beale Street.
descriptions.Blues---Modern Electric Blues: Electric blues from the 1960s onward, with blues-rock power and extended guitar solos.
descriptions.Blues---Piano Blues: Blues centered on the piano, from rowdy barrelhouse to slow, expressive ballads.
descriptions.Blues---Piedmont Blues: Southeastern fingerpicked blues with an alternating bass and a ragtime-like bounce.
descriptions.Blues---Rhythm & Blues: Early R&B: blues-based popular music with a strong backbeat, horns and vocal groups.
descriptions.Blues---Texas Blues: Texas blues, known for swinging rhythms and fluid, jazzy single-note guitar.
descriptions.Brass & Military---Brass Band: Brass and percussion ensembles, from British colliery bands to New Orleans street bands.
descriptions.Brass & Military---Marches: Strict-tempo marching pieces with bold brass, snare drums and a steady two-beat pulse.
descriptions.Brass & Military---Military: Music performed by or written for armed forces bands: anthems, bugle calls, fanfares and ceremony.
descriptions.Brass & Military---Pipe & Drum: Bagpipe bands with snare and bass drums, rooted in Scottish and Irish tradition.
descriptions.Children's---Educational: Songs and recordings that teach children letters, numbers, languages and other basics.
descriptions.Children's---Nursery Rhymes: Traditional rhymes and simple sing-along songs for young children.
descriptions.Children's---Story: Narrated stories for children, often with music and sound effects.
descriptions.Classical---Baroque: Music from about 1600 to 1750 with ornate counterpoint and harpsichord continuo, as in Bach, Handel and Vivaldi.
descriptions.Classical---Choral: Music for choir, sacred or secular, with or without accompaniment.
descriptions.Classical---Classical: Music of the Classical period, about 1750 to 1820, with balanced forms and clear melodies, as in Haydn and Mozart.
descriptions.Classical---Contemporary: Classical composition from recent decades, ranging from accessible to highly experimental.
descriptions.Classical---Early: Music from before 1600, often played on period instruments with historical performance practice.
descriptions.Classical---Impressionist: Late 19th and early 20th century music focused on color and atmosphere, as in Debussy and Ravel.
descriptions.Classical---Medieval: European music from about 500 to 1400, including plainchant, troubadour songs and early polyphony.
descriptions.Classical---Modern: Early to mid 20th century music that broke with tradition, from Stravinsky to Bartók.
descriptions.Classical---Neo-Classical: 20th century music that returns to Baroque and Classical forms and clarity with a modern ear.
descriptions.Classical---Neo-Romantic: Later music that revives the lush harmony and emotional sweep of Romanticism.
descriptions.Classical---Opera: Drama told through singing and staged with orchestra, arias and ensembles.
descriptions.Classical---Operetta: Light opera with spoken dialogue, catchy tunes and comic or romantic plots.
descriptions.Classical---Oratorio: Large works for choir, soloists and orchestra, usually on sacred themes and performed without staging.
descriptions.Classical---Post-Modern: Late 20th century music that mixes styles, quotes the past and plays with genre boundaries.
descriptions.Classical---Renaissance: Music from about 1400 to 1600 with flowing vocal polyphony, as in Josquin and Palestrina.
descriptions.Classical---Romantic: Emotional 19th century music with rich harmony and expanded orchestras, as in Chopin, Brahms and Tchaikovsky.
descriptions.Classical---Twelve-tone: Serial music built on rows of all twelve pitches, pioneered by Schoenberg and his circle.
